payload.name: description
payload.value:
When a basicly release fixes the rank-1 routing floor (basicly-vgbylo5), I want to install that release in burndown-chart and then remove every prose comment, so I can run the latest basicly gates, tracker and skills on this repository.

Install the basicly release that fixes basicly-vgbylo5, then remove every prose comment by the no-comments rules. Wait for that release: v0.20.2 is the latest tag on 2026-10-07 and does not carry the fix.

## External references

- basicly-vgbylo5: shipped skills route rank-1 below the consumer floor. The upgrade waits on this fix.
- basicly-49vecmn: `.gitignore` `*.json` hides `.basicly/ledger/template.json`.
- basicly-dvghvky: repo hooks rewrite or refuse basicly-generated files.
- basicly-3a1z7w6: `install --dry-run` fails with PENDING_GLOB. The real install works.

## Findings from the v0.20.2 attempt (2026-10-07, discarded)

1. catalog-lint refused the install commit: rank-1 routing 86.7%, below `rank1_floor = 0.891`. Do not lower the floor.
2. no-comments checks whole files: 788 of 795 code files, 22,369 prose comments. No ratchet (basicly-wfh0mkq cancelled).
3. Install moves the prefix to `.basicly/ledger/template.json`, which `*.json` ignores. Add `!.basicly/ledger/template.json` (user approved).
4. ruff --fix and ruff-format rewrote 17 generated scripts (restore with `basicly skills-build`). detect-secrets flagged 2 core skill.yaml files. markdownlint refused the projected instruction files and `.basicly/core/kit/tracker/GUIDANCE.md`. Exclude generated paths in `.pre-commit-config.yaml` (user approved).
5. The stale `snapshot.jsonl` makes fsck fail after install. Move it aside first.
6. After the upgrade, ready shows 0 until records get an INVEST/C3 review.
7. 702 "refused ... not a record id" lines from the tracker step are noise.
8. A version number in a commit subject is refused. Put it in the body.

## Findings from 2026-10-07 recovery

- The global `basicly` on PATH is 0.20.2. Run every basicly command through `uvx --from git+https://github.com/niksavis/basicly@<tag> basicly` until the upgrade lands.
- `.claude/settings.json` and `.basicly/ledger/snapshot.jsonl` are ignored, so `git reset --hard` leaves the newer copies on disk.
- `hooks-build` keeps hook entries it does not own. A stale entry to a missing script blocks every Bash call. Remove it by hand.
- The v0.12.2 tracker kit has no `fsck`.

## Order

1. Clean tree, new branch.
2. `uvx --from git+https://github.com/niksavis/basicly@<fixed tag> basicly install`, no --force.
3. Unignore template.json, add the hook excludes, move the snapshot aside, `basicly skills-build`.
4. `basicly check`, then `python3 .basicly/core/kit/tracker/cli.py fsck .basicly/ledger`.
5. Commit the install. If catalog-lint still refuses on the floor, stop and report.
6. Move facts out of comments (because, workaround, units, TODO, FIXME, HACK, bug, issue, http) into names, tests or records. Then `comments/cli.py fix` one top-level directory at a time, with tests, linters and a commit each. Watch for code that reads `__doc__`. Re-run `check` until 0.

## Acceptance

- `basicly --version` through the pinned form reports the fixed tag, and `basicly check` passes.
- `python3 .basicly/core/kit/comments/cli.py check` reports 0.
- The pytest baseline holds: 1922 passed, 5 skipped, 3 xfailed.

payload.name: requirements
payload.value:
- Install basicly v0.21.0 or later through `basicly install`; lower no floor and bypass no hook.
- Keep the repo linters off basicly-generated paths through per-hook excludes in .pre-commit-config.yaml.
- Remove prose comments one top-level directory per commit, with tests and linters green on each.
- Move a fact a comment carries into a name, a test or a record before its comment goes.

payload.text:
Facts moved out of comments, root *.py files (2026-10-08):
- validate.py COVERAGE_RATCHET_PERCENT: callbacks/ was added to coverage measurement; measured 45.82% over data, ui, visualization and 40.73% over all four (2026-09-10). The ratchet sits just below 40.73%. Raise it when coverage rises; never lower it to make a red gate pass.
- validate.py check_pip_audit: --no-deps because requirements.txt is compiled with every transitive dependency; resolution would only build a slow temporary environment.
- validate.py: on Windows npx is npx.cmd, and shutil.which("npx") may resolve npx.ps1.
- release.py RELEASE_TEST_GATE_PATH: scoped to tests/unit/ because tests/integration/ is red and order-dependent (IMP-004/005/006). Widen it to the whole suite once those are fixed. The gate exists so a tag cannot be cut against a red suite.
- release.py create_tag: must run after the version bump, changelog, version_info and metrics commits, so a tag never points to an intermediate commit.
- app.py: the JSON-to-SQLite migration (T029) must run before any workspace operation. The stale task cleanup must run before Dash accepts requests.
- regenerate_changelog.py: generates draft entries for new tags only and never overwrites an existing entry. When a scope has both feat and fix commits, the fixes are development iterations; only a fix-only scope counts as a bug fix for a released feature.
- install_hooks.py: Git for Windows provides sh.exe; the sh hook script detects the venv Python. Executable bits are set on Unix only, because git on Windows uses the shebang.

Facts moved out of comments, configuration/ (2026-10-08):
- dora_config.py DORA_BENCHMARKS: each "threshold" is in days (0.04 = under 1 hour, 1 = under 1 day). For change failure rate, lower is better and the value is a percentage.
- flow_config.py FLOW_EFFICIENCY_THRESHOLDS: below warning_threshold (15) is concerning. Most flow metrics take their status lists from project_classification. MetricsConfig has no issue-type filter for WIP. An effort category can override the flow type for Task and Story, never for Bug.
- metrics_config.py: FORECAST_TREND_THRESHOLD 0.10 is a plus-minus 10% band; FLOW_LOAD_RANGE_PERCENT 0.20 is a plus-minus 20% band for WIP bounds.
- logging_config.py SensitiveDataFilter: patterns apply in order, most specific first; the Bearer pattern must precede the generic Authorization pattern (held by test_redact_bearer_tokens). Only user data is redacted. Numeric args keep their type unless redaction happened (held by test_sensitive_data_filter_preserves_numeric_types).
- logging_config.py setup_logging: Waitress "Task queue depth" warnings are normal under load and are suppressed. shutdown_logging closes every root handler because Windows holds file locks until then.
- help_content.py: FORECAST_HELP_DETAILED was historically defined in two places and is kept for backward compatibility.
- settings.py: forecast_settings.json is the legacy settings file, kept for backward compatibility. COLOR_PALETTE "warning" is Bootstrap warning yellow #ffc107.

payload.text:
Facts moved out of comments, visualization/ (2026-10-08):
- Units: pert_time_items and pert_time_points are in days (charts.py, helpers.py). sprint_duration_seconds and total_duration are in seconds (sprint_charts/_bar_multi.py). metric_trends._add_performance_tier_zones converts MTTR elite threshold from hours to days (divide by 24); high and medium are already in days.
- Caps: data_preparation.prepare_visualization_data limits the forecast to 2 years (730 days) and 100 points per line, for performance. helpers.generate_burndown_forecast never forecasts beyond today plus 10 years. forecast_chart_layout.add_deadline_marker shades the 14 days before the deadline as the critical period.
- data_preparation.prepare_visualization_data filters by date, not by row count (.iloc); this was a deliberate fix.
- bug_charts_trend.create_bug_trend_chart (T037a): a visual warning marks 3 or more consecutive weeks where creation exceeds closure. bug_charts_forecast shows an insufficient-data annotation under 4 weeks of data.
- metric_trends: percentage, ratio and count axes never go below 0. Week order on the x axis is the explicit week_labels order.
- chart_config and metric_trends: displayModeBar is off and plot and paper backgrounds are white, never transparent, on mobile-first charts.
- sprint_cfd_chart: stack order bottom to top is Done, Testing, In Progress, To Do; traces are added in reverse so Done is the first trace. Statuses not in the order list are appended.
- sprint_charts/_health: health priority 1-5 is blocked, aging, active WIP, to do, completed.
- forecast_chart_render and helpers import some helpers inside functions to avoid a circular import.
- The TODO for create_sprint_timeline_chart is now burndownchart-a80uxx.

Facts moved out of comments, assets/ (2026-10-08):
- z-index ladder: Bootstrap modal backdrop 1055; profile selector column 1050 (above accordion items); datepicker 1060; react-select menus 1065; field-mapping dropdowns 1070; profile dropdown 1080 (fixed positioning set by JavaScript).
- dropdown-fixes.css: accordion collapse hides overflow only during the animation; accordion items and body allow overflow so a dropdown shows above the next item; the profile accordion keeps min-height 250px so its dropdown can open. SVG data URIs cannot use CSS variables, so tab icon colours are literal.
- jql_language_mode.js: CodeMirror 5 must load first (CDN in app.py), and the token CSS classes live in custom.css. Keyword priority ordering is T030.
- jql_editor_native.js: the hidden input value wins over the editor because Dash may update it. Initialization retries every 500 ms for the first 5 seconds to catch Dash dynamic content; a hidden container is marked for refresh.
- namespace_autocomplete_validation.js depends on namespace_autocomplete_data.js (window._nsa). Dash loads assets in alphabetical order.
- mobile_navigation.js: never click tab elements directly; that races Dash.
- long_press_force_refresh.js: LONG_PRESS_DURATION and update_reconnect.js POLL_INTERVAL_MS are in milliseconds (2000 = 2 seconds). The force-refresh flag is cleared by the clientside callback after it reads it.
- update_reconnect.js: polling starts only after the old server is gone, to avoid a race with a live server; it stops after 10 seconds. Toasts are cleared before the overlay goes, and a toast blocker runs for 2 seconds while Dash callbacks settle. The success toast auto-dismisses after 5 seconds. JSON responses are parsed defensively because a fallback response can be HTML.

Facts moved out of comments, callbacks/ (2026-10-08):
- accordion_settings.enforce_query_save_before_data_ops: a query must be saved before it can be executed.
- app_update.handle_manual_update_instructions: fixes a race where toast rendering blocked the overlay.
- field_mapping/auto_config.auto_configure_from_metadata: values go in the flat keys the UI dropdowns read.
- field_mapping/modal_loading: uses visibility, not display, because Bootstrap d-flex carries !important.
- field_mapping/profile_management.clear_field_mapping_state_on_profile_switch: the memory store persisted across profile switches; clearing it keeps profiles isolated.
- field_mapping/save_load.save_or_validate_mappings: order is server-side validation, then metrics cache invalidation, then save; parent_issue_types goes into field_mappings.general.
- field_mapping/state_tracking: only non-empty values are stored; namespace inputs have no server-side state tracking (clientside JS reads dcc.Input values, see namespace_autocomplete).
- field_mapping/tab_rendering.render_tab_content: merge state before the empty-state check, and only on a tab switch, not on modal open.
- field_mapping/validation_helpers: WIP statuses must not include completion statuses.
- field_value_fetch.prefetch_field_values_on_modal_open depends on the is_open output of the modal callback.
- flow_metrics_callbacks: renders only on the Flow tab.
- jira_config.save_jira_configuration_callback guards against rapid repeated clicks.
- jira_data_store.populate_jira_issues_store does not filter at store level; each consumer filters what it needs.
- jql_editor: syncs CodeMirror through clientside JS because dcc.Store cannot be updated from plain JS.
- profile_management.handle_profile_form_submit: an empty date is None, never "".
- progress_bar.update_progress_bars: 5-second grace for the backend before an error status; metrics-refresh-trigger fires once when postprocess starts; a completion older than 10 seconds is stale; success shows for 3 seconds, then hides without deleting the progress file (race).
- query_management.manage_button_states suppresses alerts triggered by the query selector during a switch (race).
- query_switching: switch_query_callback must not call switch_query(); a new query loads only on "Load Query Data"; after a switch the settings must include current scope data, or forecasts break.
- settings/helpers.calculate_remaining_work_for_data_window: the parameter panel shows current remaining work.
- settings/parameter_panel: a restart within the last 5 seconds does not restore progress.
- settings_panel.toggle_settings_panel must not fire on initial button render; backdrop visibility follows the panel states.
- statistics: prevents a save loop when the tab re-renders with database data; no statistics for dates beyond today.
- visualization.register: stored state never overrides the current statistics (an earlier fix caused query-switch bugs).
- visualization_helpers/tab_content.create_scope_tracking_tab_content: data is already filtered in the callback; do not filter again.
- import_export and version_update_notification toasts stay 20 seconds (20000 ms) so a user can read and click them.

payload.text:
Facts moved out of comments, ui/ (2026-10-08):
- Units: toast_notifications duration and tooltip delay/base_delay are in milliseconds (0 = no auto-dismiss). tooltip_utils_core.cache_tooltip_content ttl is in seconds (default 300).
- styles.py is the aggregation shim for ui.styles. Do not migrate callers away from it; the callers span all of ui/.
- jql_editor: CodeMirror 6 loads via CDN in app.py external_scripts; assets/jql_editor_init.js and jql_language_mode.js must exist; .cm-jql-* token classes live in assets/custom.css. The dbc.Textarea is the source of truth for callbacks and stays visible, because Dash callbacks need visible inputs; CodeMirror is cosmetic and degrades gracefully. ScriptRunner function names match exactly.
- layout.create_app_layout: the sticky header must be the first visible element; the fixed-position element must sit outside the card.
- tabs.create_tab_content never falls back to another tab's content, to avoid React hooks errors.
- dashboard: shows current remaining work, not windowed scope. Statistics are weekly (Mondays), so the latest Monday row is current. throughput_analytics: the project dashboard computes velocity ad hoc from project_statistics. insights_engine_rendering: scope growth uses the same filtered window as the charts.
- dashboard_enhanced/stats._calculate_confidence_intervals computes true statistical confidence intervals.
- parameter_panel: count unique dates, not rows, to avoid inflation from duplicate dates. panel_controller passes total_items and total_points as both scope and remaining values.
- scope_metrics/_dashboard: total_items_scope and total_points_scope are the initial scope at the period start; the baseline comes from the callback.
- work_distribution_card thresholds: feature work below 40% is critical; defects above 40%, tech debt above 20% and risk above 10% are critical. For defect, tech debt and risk, low is good.
- budget_cards/core_metrics: utilization 95-100%+ is critical (red); runway under 4 weeks is critical. Cost sparklines never go below 0.
- cards/settings_helpers: never raise to the caller.
- The data_cards table split TODO is now burndownchart-ob0exv. The unused mobile bottom sheet is now burndownchart-i2sim7.

payload.acceptance_criteria:
- get_affected_weeks_from_changed_issues includes the weeks of changelog status transitions
- A regression test fails before the fix and passes after it
payload.description:
When a delta fetch sees an issue whose status changed without a new created or resolved date, I want its affected weeks recalculated, so I can trust the weekly statistics after an incremental refresh.

data/jira/delta_fetch.py get_affected_weeks_from_changed_issues derives the affected weeks from created and resolved dates only. A removed TODO said it should also check changelog status transitions. A status change that moves an issue in or out of WIP or flow without changing those dates leaves its weeks stale. Not reproduced yet; the comment removal (burndownchart-xjl0x1) surfaced it.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Load a query, then move one issue to an in-progress status in Jira without resolving it.
2. Run the delta refresh.
3. Compare the weekly flow statistics with a full refresh of the same query.
payload.requirements: - A delta refresh and a full refresh give the same weekly statistics for the same Jira state
payload.title: Delta fetch ignores status transitions when it picks the weeks to recalculate

data/migration/schema_manager.py initialize_schema accepts force but never drops a table; a removed TODO said DROP TABLE statements were still needed. The comment removal (burndownchart-xjl0x1) surfaced it.

payload.text:
Facts moved out of comments, data/ (2026-10-08):
- Units: CACHE_EXPIRATION_HOURS 24; DEFAULT_TTL_SECONDS 3600 (1 hour). RATE_LIMIT_REFILL_INTERVAL_SECONDS, INITIAL_RETRY_DELAY_SECONDS (doubles each retry) and UPDATE_CHECK_TIMEOUT_SECONDS now carry their unit in the name. report/domain_metrics: the health calculator expects lead time in hours, not days, under the key lead_time.
- Parents (epics) are stored but never counted; every metric filters parent issues dynamically, never by the literal "Epic" (active_work_manager, jira/epic_fetch, jira/scope_sync).
- Budget: budget_settings is current after revisions; never replay revisions (double-counts deltas) in budget_calculator_core._get_current_budget or budget_calculator_consumption.calculate_budget_consumed.
- Windows: filter by date range, never by row count (.iloc), in processing_dashboard, processing_statistics, processing_weekly_forecast, scope_metrics. processing_averages: data_points_count means weeks, capped to the available weeks; items come from the flow_velocity metric snapshots so they match Flow Velocity exactly. report/data_loader matches week labels to the app's selected window.
- processing_rates.calculate_rates drops zero-value weeks before any calculation (they often come from _fill_missing_weeks); valid_pert_factor is an int. processing_daily_forecast never forecasts beyond today plus 10 years.
- report/dashboard_metrics must match the app (data/processing.py, ui/dashboard): statistics are incremental, so sum, never .iloc[-1]; filter to weeks_count before health and velocity; weekly rows are Mondays; keep the sign for health; confidence matches ui/dashboard exactly. generator_recommendations uses the insights_engine method.
- scope_metrics: baseline parameters are the initial scope at the period start; created items are not in the baseline; completed items are not added (double count).
- config_validation: active statuses must be a subset of WIP; WIP must exclude completion statuses; only the Flow baseline fields are required.
- Field detection: date fields must be datetime; points must be a number; sprint needs data in at least 10% of sampled issues, parent in at least 5%; Jira checkboxes appear as type "string"; reject fields holding Java class names or complex objects.
- Jira fetch: include fixVersions (DORA lead time) and project (DevOps vs development filter) in the fields; strip "=Value" filter syntax from field ids; changelog uses the field display name, so check both name and id; changelog is filtered to status transitions; ORDER BY stays at the end of the JQL; scope_sync must build the same fields string as fetch_jira_issues; save issues before fetching changelog; invalidate the changelog cache on every Jira fetch; read profile and query ids before the fetch (race); recalculate when settings changed even with no new data. The data cache key excludes field mappings. CHANGELOG_CACHE_VERSION 2.0 added the DORA fields.
- dora/_deploy_frequency counts operational tasks from DevOps projects only; dora_metrics_calculator saves only when there is no error_state. Operational tasks never reach flow_type_classifier.get_flow_type.
- Persistence: update_project_scope updates scope only and never overwrites statistics, with a safety check against saving loaded defaults. save_statistics ensures week_label; load_statistics drops duplicate legacy dates; save_unified_project_data normalizes stat_date to YYYY-MM-DD (unnormalized dates made duplicate rows). JSONBackend is legacy; new code uses SQLiteBackend. data/processing.py is an aggregation shim; do not migrate callers away from it.
- task_progress: mark complete only when actually done (not in an unfinished fetch phase); status "complete" must match callbacks/progress_bar.py.
- Import: an imported profile must re-verify its Jira connection and field mappings; local credentials are never overwritten.
- bug_insights default thresholds: bug capacity 30% warning, 40% critical; resolution time 14 days warning, 30 days critical. bug_processing: the last ISO week holds at least 4 days of the year.
- profile_manager: P
